vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: here-now
Version: 1.6.7

The here-now skill bundle provides a legitimate utility for deploying static files and directories to the here.now hosting service. The core logic in scripts/publish.sh implements a standard three-step upload process (create, upload to presigned URLs, finalize) and includes security best practices such as a safety guard to prevent sending API keys to non-default base URLs. The SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md files provide clear instructions for agent-assisted authentication and credential management using a dedicated local file (~/.herenow/credentials), with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's functionality (uploading/publishing files to an external here.now service) matches its description, but there are metadata/instruction inconsistencies and several operational details you should verify before trusting it with files or credentials.

dimensions.detail: The skill's declared purpose (static file hosting/publishing) matches the included script: it builds a manifest and uploads files to https://here.now. However the registry metadata claims no required binaries or env vars while SKILL.md and the script require curl, file, jq and optionally read $HERENOW_API_KEY and ~/.herenow/credentials. This metadata mismatch is incoherent and worth verifying (typo or packaging error).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and the script will read/write local files (~/.herenow/credentials and .herenow/state.json in the working directory) and will upload arbitrary files to an external service. The SKILL.md also instructs the agent to request a one-time sign-in code from here.now by sending the user's email, and to store the returned API key locally. Reading/storing claim tokens and credentials is expected for this feature, but it broadens scope beyond a pure 'formatting' or local helper skill — the agent (and user) must be aware that data is transmitted off-host.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no install spec), but SKILL.md recommends an npx install (npx skills add heredotnow/skill ...). The script can fall back to recommending running a remote installer to get jq (curl https://here.now/install.sh | bash) if jq is missing. Suggesting remote install scripts is a moderate risk and should be audited before executing. The script also references a bundled jq at bin/jq that is not included in the provided file list, which is inconsistent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script optionally consumes $HERENOW_API_KEY (and can accept an --api-key flag) and reads ~/.herenow/credentials; yet the registry metadata declared no required env vars or credentials. The skill also auto-loads claim tokens from .herenow/state.json in the working directory (these tokens are effectively secrets for anonymous artifacts). Asking for the user's email to request a sign-in code (agent-assisted sign-up) is also sensitive. The number and type of local secrets accessed are proportionate to a publishing service, but the metadata omission is suspicious and should be corrected/confirmed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request system-wide or always-on privileges. It writes a local state file (.herenow/state.json) in the current working directory and can store a credentials file at ~/.herenow/credentials; this is normal for a client that persists keys. It does not modify other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will upload whatever files you give it to an external service (here.now) and can store credentials locally (~/.herenow/credentials) and a local state cache (.herenow/state.json). Before installing or running: 1) Confirm the skill/package origin (the SKILL.md's npx install path and registry metadata are inconsistent). 2) Review here.now's privacy/security policy and confirm you trust the service to hold your files and any API key. 3) Do not publish sensitive secrets or private data; anonymous publishes expire in 24h but claim tokens are returned only once. 4) Avoid passing API keys on the command line; use the credentials file as recommended. 5) Audit any remote install commands the README suggests (curl | bash) and the npm package (if you run the npx command) before executing. If you need to be extra cautious, run the script in an isolated environment and test with non-sensitive files first.
llm.findings: [pre-scan-injection-none] expected: Static scanner reported no injection signals. That absence doesn't guarantee safety: the script sends arbitrary user files to an external API (expected), so manual review of the destination and install commands is still recommended.
